label: OFFLINE EVALUATION ONLY. Classical detectors on synthetic generated covers. A low AUC is NOT evidence of undetectability.

basic.name: spam1[49]
basic.definition: first-order co-occurrence of horizontally/vertically adjacent pixel differences truncated to [-3,3], averaged over both directions and all channels (7x7 normalised counts)

basic.name: lsb_ones
basic.definition: fraction of ones in the least-significant bit plane

basic.name: lsb_corr_h / lsb_corr_v
basic.definition: correlation of the LSB plane with its right / lower neighbour

basic.name: pov_chi2
basic.definition: pairs-of-values chi-square statistic of the histogram, divided by the number of populated pairs

basic.name: hcf_com
basic.definition: centre of mass of the histogram characteristic function (|DFT| of the 256-bin histogram)

basic.name: hist_smooth
basic.definition: mean absolute second difference of the normalised histogram

basic.name: hp_std / hp_mad / hp_kurt
basic.definition: standard deviation, mean absolute value and kurtosis of a 3x3 high-pass (KV-style) residual

basic.name: d1_std / d1_kurt
basic.definition: standard deviation and kurtosis of first differences

basic.name: block8
basic.definition: 8x8 blockiness: mean |difference| across block boundaries divided by the same inside blocks

basic.name: parity_run
basic.definition: mean run length of equal LSBs along rows

features.srm_lite: SRM-inspired: residuals d1 (first difference, q=1), d2 (second difference, q=2), d3 (third difference, q=3) and kb (3x3 KB high-pass, q=4), quantised and truncated to [-2, 2]; third-order co-occurrence of horizontally and vertically adjacent residual triples, symmetrised under sign flip and reversal (39 classes per residual), normalised, averaged over directions and channels. A small subset of the spatial rich model, not the SRM itself.

detectors.lr_basic: L2 logistic regression (l2 = 1, NumPy, Newton/IRLS) on the basic features
detectors.lr_srm: L2 logistic regression (l2 = 10, NumPy, Newton/IRLS) on basic + srm-lite features
detectors.trees_srm: extremely randomised trees (scikit-learn ExtraTreesClassifier, 500 trees, min_samples_leaf 2, seed 0) on basic + srm-lite features

protocol.splits: seed namespaces train / val / test (disjoint); detectors are trained on train and evaluated once on test; val is used only for the risk table
protocol.pairing: a cover and its stego image share a seed and a split
protocol.confidence_intervals: percentile bootstrap, 1000 resamples of test seeds
protocol.tpr_at_1pct_fpr: largest threshold with cover FPR <= 1 %; resolution 1 / #test covers
protocol.payload: uniformly random bytes (ciphertext-like); carrier bits and value streams random (indistinguishable from the real ones)
protocol.hyperparameters: fixed a priori (see detectors); nothing tuned on the test split

limitations: Synthetic procedural covers only; no photographs. Results do not transfer to natural images.
Small samples (tens of covers per family): confidence intervals are wide; differences inside an interval are not meaningful.

Detectors are small classical models on hand-made features (a subset of SRM-style residual co-occurrences); full rich models with ensemble classifiers and CNN steganalysers are stronger. No CNN was trained: no deep-learning framework is available here.
An adversary who knows the generator can produce unlimited training covers; these detectors train on a small sample.
The single-algorithm conditions embed over the whole image without the carrier; the operational transport is the transport_* conditions.
Confidence intervals reflect sampling of test seeds only, not model or feature choice.
